haiku-low.q1: Lookups use sub, so the user still signs in to the same account. Google never changes users.email, so the old address stays stored.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter that account's password on the confirmation form. A correct password links Google and creates the session. Refused if the user already has another Google account.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password gives a generic message and adds one failed login. At the fifth, the account locks for 15 minutes and the pending link is deleted.
haiku-low.q4: A verified unmatched email creates a user with a NULL password, links the sub in one transaction, and signs in. An unverified email is refused and nothing is created.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt expired after 600 seconds, or was already consumed by GETDEL. The error page shows, the cookie is cleared, and nothing else changes.
haiku-low.q6: It creates a new sessions row, as password login does, and sets a new sid cookie. The browser's old sid session row is deleted, even one for another user.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required, only a valid session. If the Google account is linked to another user, settings shows 'account used elsewhere' and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: The browser holds state in goauth_state. Redis holds the nonce and PKCE verifier under the state's SHA-256. GETDEL at the first matching callback removes them, or the 600-second TTL does.
haiku-low.q9: Redis holds goauth:pending:<random id> with sub, user, and next. The browser holds only the random id in goauth_pending. Success, lock, failed re-check, expired POST, or 600-second TTL deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In Postgres table google_identities. Sub is its primary key, so one row per Google account. user_id is UNIQUE, so one Google account per user.
haiku-low.q11: The user sees an error page to start again. The attempt is consumed and the cookie cleared, with no tokens kept. The document does not say the exchange is retried; it says a timeout is handled like a bad token.
haiku-low.q12: The attempt record stores the mode, and GETDEL returns it. Settings mode requires the sid cookie to equal the attempt's session id, with an unexpired row; that row's user is the linking user.

sonnet.q1: Nothing special: lookups use `sub`, not email, so the changed Google email still reaches the same account (Google never changes users.email). If the user isn't locked (locked_until in future), start_session runs and they are signed in.
sonnet.q2: They must prove ownership with the account's password. A pending link is created (Redis, 600 s TTL, goauth_pending cookie) and a password form is shown; POST /auth/google/confirm with a correct bcrypt password (user not locked, and a transaction re-check that U still has no Google account and sub is still unlinked) inserts the google_identities link, sets email_verified_at if null, deletes the pending link, then start_session.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins and shows a generic wrong-password message; the pending link stays until its 10 minutes end. At the fifth wrong password, locked_until = now + 15 min and failed_logins resets to 0; the pending link is deleted (half-finished link thrown away) and 'Account temporarily locked' is shown. No link is created.
sonnet.q4: If email_verified is true and no user matches the lowercased email: in one transaction, insert a new user (email lowercased, password_hash NULL, email_verified_at now) and the google_identities link, then start_session (signed in). If email_verified is false: refuse, telling them to sign in with email and password; nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: At 12 minutes the attempt (Redis TTL 600 s) has expired, and a second load finds it already consumed by GETDEL. Either way (provided the state param matches the goauth_state cookie) the attempt is not found, so the error page 'link unknown, expired or used' is shown and the cookie is cleared; nothing else changes. If the cookie has also expired/missing (Max-Age 600 s), the state check fails first: error page, nothing changes.
sonnet.q6: The same session as a password login, via start_session: delete the sessions row for the browser's existing sid cookie (if any, even for a different user), INSERT a new sessions row, set the sid cookie, redirect to next if relative path else /home. Sessions in other browsers are unaffected.
sonnet.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required; only a valid signed-in session (the sid cookie must equal the attempt's session id and that session unexpired). If the sub is already linked to another user, it redirects to settings with 'account used elsewhere' and nothing changes. (Also: already linked to this user gives 'already linked'; if the user has a different Google account linked, refuse.) No new session on success.
sonnet.q8: The nonce and PKCE verifier (with the mode, next, and settings session id) are in the Redis attempt record at goauth:attempt:<sha256 of state>, TTL 600 s. The raw state is held only in the browser's goauth_state cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/auth/google, Max-Age 600 s) and the Google redirect parameter. The attempt is removed by GETDEL at the first callback with a matching cookie, or by TTL; the cookie is cleared by the callback after its cookie check passes, or by expiry.
sonnet.q9: In Redis at goauth:pending:<random id>, storing sub, user U and next, TTL 600 s from the callback (not extended by retries). The browser refers to it via the goauth_pending cookie holding the random id (same attributes as the state cookie). It is deleted on success, on lock, on a failed re-check, on an expired POST, or by TTL; the cookie is cleared along with it.
sonnet.q10: In Postgres table google_identities(sub PK, user_id UNIQUE, linked_at), with user_id referencing users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. The sub primary key gives one user per Google account, and the UNIQUE on user_id gives one Google account per user.
sonnet.q11: The user sees an error page 'could not finish with Google' and must start again. The exchange is not retried: it is one HTTP call with a fixed timeout, a timeout counts as a failure, and there is no second pass. The attempt is consumed, the cookie cleared, and no tokens are kept.
sonnet.q12: The attempt record stored in Redis at start includes the mode (login or settings); the callback gets it from the GETDEL of the attempt. For settings mode, the attempt also stores the session id: the request's sid cookie must equal it and that sessions row must exist and be unexpired, and the linking user is that session row's user. If the check fails, redirect to login with a neutral message and nothing is linked.
